programs.name: Alabama AGELINE (Aging and Disability Resource Centers)
programs.description: A statewide line that connects you to the Area Agency on Aging and Aging and Disability Resource Center for your county: meals, in-home services, transportation, caregiver support and senior legal assistance. Military service is not required.
programs.next_step: Call 800-243-5463 (1-800-AGE-LINE) from anywhere in Alabama. Choose a county above for the direct number of its Area Agency on Aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

programs.name: Alabama Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program
programs.organization: Alabama Office of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman, Department of Senior Services
programs.description: Statewide advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and other long-term care facilities, delivered through 13 regional ombudsman programs.
programs.next_step: Choose your county for its regional ombudsman, or call the state ombudsman office at 334-242-5753. To report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation of an adult, call the Adult Abuse Hotline at 800-458-7214. For immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing or enforcement agency.

programs.name: Legal Services Alabama
programs.description: Free civil legal help for people with low income and for adults 60 and older. A VA-funded program helps veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness. Not criminal defense.
programs.next_step: Call the intake line (English 866-456-4995; Spanish 888-835-3505) or apply at legalservicesalabama.org. Have your county and the legal problem ready, and say if you are a veteran.
constraints: Applicants are screened; income, case type and capacity limits apply. The veterans program serves veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness. Phone lines are open Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m.

programs.name: VA medical centers serving Alabama
programs.description: Birmingham VA Health Care System: Birmingham VA Medical Center (205-933-8101). Central Alabama Veterans Health Care System: Montgomery campus (334-272-4670) and Tuskegee campus (334-727-0550). Tuscaloosa VA Medical Center (205-554-2000). Community clinics are listed in VA’s facility locator.
programs.next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic and its medical center. Not enrolled yet? Ask your Veterans Service Officer for help applying.
constraints: VA does not publish county lists for these systems in the pages read, so this card does not assign counties. Your VA care team may be at a different clinic or system; follow what VA tells you.

coverage_scope: Referral edition. All 67 counties have a Veterans Service Office (some shared), a matched Area Agency on Aging and a regional long-term-care ombudsman.
coverage_note: Veterans Service Office addresses, phones and hours come from the Alabama Department of Veterans Affairs office list; where the list groups counties under one office, each county shows that office, and the Montgomery hours and Covington address follow the department’s 2026 announcements. Area Agencies on Aging, their counties and phones come from the Alabama Department of Senior Services. Regional ombudsman cards show the Area Agency on Aging main line that hosts the program; the state ombudsman page lists no regional numbers, and the National Consumer Voice directory (undated) names the host agencies. Centers for Independent Living and their counties come from a member-center directory and the ILRU national directory. Reviewed November 15, 2026. Contacts are not telephone-confirmed.
